United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

description.narrative: Pakistan is a member of the Greening Education Partnership and ‘greening education’ is one of UNESCO Islamabad’s priority programme areas. UNESCO Islamabad’s approach to greening education is a whole-of-sector approach, seeking to integrate more sustainable practices across the education system. In line with this, UNESCO is currently facilitating a review of ESD and GCED integration in Pakistan’s primary and secondary education curriculum. Acknowledging the interconnected nature of ESD and STEM, UNESCO is also supporting the dissemination of science kits to selected secondary schools across Pakistan. An upcoming initiative will further enhance teachers’ capacities in delivering science and math subjects, with a particular emphasis on fostering play-based and experiential science learning, incorporating essential concepts related to sustainability and climate change. This multifaceted approach underscores UNESCO's commitment to advancing environmentally conscious and innovative education practices in Pakistan. Furthermore, in early 2023, UNESCO commissioned a Damage and Needs Assessment for the Ziarat Juniper Biosphere Reserve. This assessment aimed to evaluate the magnitude of damage resulting from the unprecedented rainfall and flooding experienced in 2022. As part of the recommendations, the study emphasized the need for increased advocacy, awareness, and educational efforts aimed at promoting the conservation of the forest's natural resources, with the goal of sensitizing communities on a broader scale. This recommendation also serves as a significant factor in proposing the ZJBR as a pilot site for climate change and sustainability education.
